x: A constitutional body is one set up and empowered by the Constitution itself, such as the ECI or the CAG. A body created by law is statutory, and one created by executive order is extra-constitutional.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Planning Commission (1950) was set up by a Cabinet resolution, so it was extra-constitutional and non-statutory. NITI Aayog (2015) and the NDC (1952) were also set up by executive action.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: Both are true: a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature, and the NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are examples.
t: Recall examples of statutory bodies.

x: The Attorney General is under Article 76, the Advocate General 165, the CAG 148, and the Finance Commission 280. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall Articles 76, 148, 165 and 280.

x: Both are true: the Attorney General serves at the President's pleasure and must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge. The qualification does not explain the tenure, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a qualification explains a tenure.

x: The Governor appoints the State's Advocate General, who must be qualified to be a High Court judge.
t: Pair the Attorney General (President) with the Advocate General (Governor).

x: I, II and III are correct: the CAG is under Article 148, appointed by the President, and removed like a Supreme Court judge. IV is false because the CAG serves six years or to age 65.
t: Recall the CAG's six-year or age-65 tenure.

x: State Finance Commissions are under Articles 243-I and 243-Y, State Election Commissions 243-K and 243-ZA, the ECI 324, and the SC Commission 338. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the Article for each commission.

x: Under Article 317, members of both the UPSC and State PSCs can be removed only by the President, after a Supreme Court inquiry. The Governor appoints State PSC members but cannot remove them.
t: Discriminate who appoints a State PSC member from who removes them.

x: Both are true: the Finance Commission has five members because it has a Chairman and four others, whose qualifications Parliament sets by law. R explains A.
t: Ask whether one Chairman plus four explains five members.

x: The ST Commission is under Article 338-A, the Backward Classes Commission 338-B, the linguistic minorities officer 350-B, and the SC Commission 338. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the order of Articles 338, 338-A and 338-B.

x: A is true: the State Election Commission conducts local elections. B is false because it comes under Articles 243-K and 243-ZA; Article 324 is the ECI.
t: Discriminate Article 324 (ECI) from 243-K and 243-ZA (State commissions).

x: I, II and III are constitutional bodies: the ECI (Article 324), the PSCs (Article 315) and the Finance Commission (Article 280). The Central Information Commission is statutory, under the RTI Act, 2005.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: Both are true: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under Section 15 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, while the Inter-State Council rests on Article 263. That difference in basis is why they are distinct, so R explains A.
t: Discriminate the statutory Zonal Councils from the constitutional Inter-State Council.

x: The Planning Commission came in 1950, the NDC in 1952, the Inter-State Council in 1990 and NITI Aayog in 2015. The order is C, B, D, A.
t: Recall the years 1950, 1952, 1990 and 2015.

x: Three are statutory: the NHRC (1993 Act), the Zonal Councils (1956 Act) and the Lokpal and Lokayuktas (2013 Act). NITI Aayog was set up by Cabinet resolution.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: The NHRC comes from the 1993 Act, the NGT from the 2010 Act, the CVC from the 2003 Act, and NITI Aayog from a Cabinet resolution of 1 January 2015. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each body to its founding Act or order.

x: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It has no Article of the Constitution behind it.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: A State Election Commissioner can be removed only in the same way as a High Court judge.
t: Discriminate the two removal safeguards.

x: The CEC can be removed only in the same way as a Supreme Court judge (Article 324(5)).
t: Discriminate the two removal safeguards.

x: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes sends its annual reports to the President, who has them laid before Parliament.
t: Recall where commission reports go.

x: The Law Commission is set up from time to time by executive order, so it is extra-constitutional. The SC Commission, Finance Commission and State Election Commission are constitutional.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: Both are true: the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is a separate constitutional body (Article 338-A) because the 89th Amendment (2003) split it from the SC Commission. R explains A.
t: Recall the 89th Amendment's split.

x: Both are true: the linguistic minorities officer reports to the President, and the post was added by the 7th Amendment (1956). How the post was created does not explain where it reports, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether how a post was created explains where it reports.

x: A is true: the State Finance Commission reviews the finances of Panchayats and municipalities. B is false because the Governor constitutes it, not the President.
t: Pair the Union Finance Commission (President) with the State one (Governor).

x: Both are true: the 89th Amendment (2003) split the ST Commission from the SC Commission, and the 102nd (2018) gave the Backward Classes Commission constitutional status.
t: Recall the 89th and 102nd Amendments.

x: I and III are correct: the Attorney General is under Article 76 and the ST Commission under 338-A. II is false because the Central Information Commission is statutory, under the RTI Act.
t: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

x: The CAG serves six years or to 65, the State Finance Commission is set up every five years, a State Election Commissioner is removed like a High Court judge, and the CEC like a Supreme Court judge. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each office to its tenure or removal rule.

x: The linguistic minorities officer came with the 7th Amendment (1956), the ST Commission split with the 89th (2003), and the Backward Classes Commission's status (Article 338-B) with the 102nd (2018). A and D both describe the 2018 change, so the order is B, C, A, D.
t: Note that two items describe the same 2018 event.

x: The NHRC and State commissions come from the 1993 Act, the Lokpal from the 2013 Act, the NGT from the 2010 Act, and the CIC from the RTI Act, 2005. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each body to its founding Act.

x: The Union Home Minister chairs all the Zonal Councils.
t: Recall who chairs the Zonal Councils.

x: Both are true: the State Finance Commission recommends how the State should share revenue with local bodies, reporting to the Governor, and the NGT is a statutory body created in 2010.
t: Recall the State Finance Commission's role.

x: Both are true: the Inter-State Council rests on Article 263, and it was set up in May 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice. The date does not explain the Article, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a date explains a constitutional basis.

x: All four are correct: the Law Commission, the NDC (6 August 1952), the Planning Commission (15 March 1950) and NITI Aayog (1 January 2015) were all set up by executive order or Cabinet resolution.
t: Recall the dates of the executive bodies.

x: All four are correct: the President appoints the Attorney General and the Finance Commission, and the Governor appoints the Advocate General and the State Election Commissioner.
t: Match each office to who appoints it.

x: Both are true: Article 315 provides for the UPSC and State PSCs, and the President and Governor appoint their members. Who appoints does not explain which Article governs, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether who appoints explains which Article governs.

x: All five are appointed by the President: the Election Commissioners, the SC, ST and Backward Classes Commissions, and the linguistic minorities officer.
t: Recall the bodies the President appoints.

x: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body under Article 280, in Part XII. Article 275 deals with grants and 282 with discretionary grants.
t: Recall Article 280.

x: Option C is incorrect: under Article 281, the President, not the Finance Minister, has the Finance Commission's report laid before both Houses, with a note on action taken.
t: Recall who lays the Finance Commission's report.

x: Both are true: the Finance Commission has five members (Article 280(1)), and Parliament sets their qualifications by law (Article 280(2)). These are separate clauses, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two separate clauses explain each other.

x: K.C. Neogy chaired the first Finance Commission, Y.V. Reddy the 14th, and N.K. Singh the 15th. The Governor appoints the State Finance Commission. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the Finance Commission chairmen.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Finance Commission recommends how to share taxes between the Centre and States, how to divide the States' share, and the principles for grants. IV is false because Article 131 disputes go to the Supreme Court.
t: Find the function that belongs to the Supreme Court.

x: Both are true: Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid to States, and Article 282 allows discretionary grants for any public purpose.
t: Discriminate Article 275 (statutory grants) from 282 (discretionary grants).

x: The President sets up a Finance Commission every five years, or earlier if needed. The interval is not rigidly fixed.
t: Recall the 'five years or earlier' rule.

x: Both are true: the 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share of divisible taxes from 32% to 42%, and recommending that share is the Commission's core task. R explains A.
t: Recall the 14th Finance Commission's 42%.

x: Three are Finance Commission Articles: 275 (grants), 280 (the Commission) and 281 (its report). Article 360 is the Financial Emergency.
t: Find the Article about the Financial Emergency.

x: A is false: the Finance Commission is not permanent; it is set up every five years or earlier. R is true: it is an independent body.
t: Discriminate a periodic body from a permanent one.

x: Both are true: the first Finance Commission was set up by Presidential order in 1951 and began work on 6 April 1952 under K.C. Neogy.
t: Recall the first Finance Commission.

x: I and IV are correct: the President appoints the members, and Parliament sets their qualifications by law. II and III are false because neither the President nor the Cabinet fixes qualifications.
t: Discriminate who appoints from who prescribes qualifications.

x: Both are true: the Finance Commission has civil-court powers to summon people and to require documents. These are two parallel powers, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two parallel powers explain each other.

x: All four are correct: the Finance Commission suggests ways to strengthen a State's Consolidated Fund to help Panchayats and municipalities, based on the State Finance Commission's recommendations.
t: Recall the Finance Commission's local-bodies role.

x: Besides sharing taxes and grants, the Finance Commission handles any other matter the President refers to it in the interest of sound finance. It does not settle legal disputes.
t: Recall the Finance Commission's residual function.

x: The State Finance Commission is under Articles 243-I and 243-Y, in Parts IX and IX-A. It deals with sharing between the State and local bodies, both Panchayats and municipalities. The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Recall the State Finance Commission's Articles.

x: Both are true: the State Finance Commission is set up every five years, and its report goes to the Governor and then to the State Legislature.
t: Recall where the State Finance Commission reports.

x: The 14th Finance Commission, under Y.V. Reddy, covered 2015–20.
t: Recall the 14th Commission's period.

x: I, II and III are correct: the 15th Finance Commission covered 2020–26 in two reports, the first for 2020–21. IV is false because 2015–20 was the 14th Commission's period.
t: Discriminate the 14th Commission's period from the 15th's.

x: Article 148 covers the CAG, 266 the Consolidated Fund, 267 the Contingency Fund, and 269A IGST. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall Articles 148, 266, 267 and 269A.

x: All three are correct: Article 269A covers IGST, added by the 101st Amendment (GST), and Article 270 covers taxes shared between the Centre and States.
t: Recall Articles 269A and 270.

x: The 15th Finance Commission's second report covered 2021–26. The first covered 2020–21.
t: Discriminate the 15th Commission's two reports.

x: Option D is incorrect: the Rajya Sabha's Deputy Chairman, not its Chairman, sits on the NHRC selection committee. The Prime Minister chairs the six-member committee, and the President appoints on its advice.
t: Recall the NHRC selection committee's members.

x: Both are true: the NHRC is statutory, not constitutional, because it was created by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. R explains A.
t: Ask whether its founding Act explains its statutory status.

x: Both are true: the President appoints the NHRC and the Governor a State Human Rights Commission. The NHRC covers Union and Concurrent List matters, and the State commission State and Concurrent List matters.
t: Discriminate the NHRC's reach from a State commission's.

x: I and II are correct: the NHRC has civil-court powers in inquiries and can visit jails. III and IV are false because its recommendations are only advisory, and it cannot directly investigate the armed forces.
t: Remember that the NHRC can only recommend.

x: The President appoints the NHRC and the Governor the State commission. The Prime Minister heads the NHRC selection panel and the Chief Minister the State one. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Pair each Union office with its State parallel.

x: Three are correct: the NHRC works at national level, State commissions at State level, and Human Rights Courts give speedy trials in districts. Statement 4 is false because the NHRC is national.
t: Recall the three levels under the 1993 Act.

x: For the armed forces, the NHRC cannot investigate directly. It asks the Central Government for a report and makes recommendations on it.
t: Recall the NHRC's limited role over the armed forces.

x: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 came into force on 28 September 1993.
t: Recall 28 September 1993.

x: Both are true: human rights mean rights to life, liberty, equality and dignity, guaranteed by the Constitution or international covenants and enforceable by Indian courts.
t: Recall the Act's definition of human rights.

x: The NHRC is chaired by a former Chief Justice of India or Supreme Court judge, and has judicial members, expert members and ex-officio members. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the NHRC's composition.

x: Three are on the NHRC selection committee: the Home Minister and the Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses. The Rajya Sabha Chairman is not; its Deputy Chairman is.
t: Recall the NHRC selection committee's members.

x: All five are the NHRC's civil-court powers: summoning and examining witnesses on oath, discovering and requiring documents, and requisitioning public records.
t: Recall the NHRC's civil-court powers.

x: Both are true: the NHRC inquires into human rights violations and also into officials' negligence in preventing them. These are two parallel functions, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two parallel functions explain each other.

x: Both are true: the NHRC spreads human rights awareness and encourages NGOs working in the field.
t: Recall the NHRC's promotional functions.

x: All four are correct: Section 2(m) of the Act defines 'armed forces' as the naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union.
t: Recall Section 2(m).
